body.x: In XR classes built on individual headsets, each learner wears an HMD. Prolonged use can cause fatigue and create hygiene and device management burdens.

Best Tech. Inc., an education and training technology company led by Woo-seung Seo, exhibited EduSpace at the 57th Korea Electronics Show (KES 2026), held from Oct. 13 to 16 at COEX in Seoul. EduSpace is an XR-based education and training platform designed for schools, public institutions and training organizations. The company used the show to identify overseas educational institutions, public-sector organizations and local education and technology partners.

EduSpace connects PC-based XR devices with existing educational infrastructure such as interactive displays and tablets, so that instructors and multiple learners can take part in immersive learning and training together. The platform offers about 100 immersive content titles covering K-12 and higher education, vocational training, industrial safety, maintenance and defense.

The key differentiator is a shared learning environment that reduces reliance on individual HMDs. Best Tech. Inc. says this lowers the fatigue, hygiene management and device operation burdens that come with prolonged HMD use, and lets institutions use the PCs, interactive displays and tablets they already have. The company also provides integrated services covering content development, platform deployment, device integration, installation, training and operational support.

Founded in 2006, Best Tech now develops education and training technologies spanning XR and AI transformation (AX). It provides immersive learning platforms and AI-powered personalized learning solutions. Its core business areas are XR education and training content, immersive learning platforms, AI-based learning and career solutions, and digital training systems for industrial and public sectors. The company combines XR content production with AI-driven analytics in education and training settings, and says its strengths are scalability across diverse devices and existing educational infrastructure, personalized learning and feedback technologies, and experience developing and deploying immersive content in education, public-sector and industrial environments.

Best Tech recorded revenue of KRW 15.95 billion in 2025, up 28.15% from the previous year. In Korea, it has supplied XR and AI-based education solutions, including EduSpace, to more than 100 schools and educational institutions. Its projects have covered K-12 and higher education, career education, vocational training, industrial safety and maintenance. Its awards include the IIOE Pioneer Award 2025 and the Prime Minister's Commendation at K-INNO SHOW 2025.

Overseas, Best Tech has built experience in the Philippines, Vietnam and Uzbekistan. In the Philippines, it set up a local presence in 2025 and is pursuing smart classroom projects and AX-based education solutions for educational institutions in Muntinlupa. It is also expanding into vocational education and training through cooperation with local organizations including TESDA, and continues to expand its digital education network through collaboration with UNESCO-ICHEI.

In Central Asia, the company is scheduled to take part in an ODA project in Uzbekistan in 2027. At the first Korea-Central Asia Business Summit in September 2026, it signed separate MOUs with CEAL.KG LLC and the DEMILGE.KG Public Foundation of Kyrgyzstan for cooperation in education technology and international education projects. It is also working with UNESCO-ICHEI on AI- and XR-based education cooperation models suited to the educational environments of Central Asian countries.

Going forward, Best Tech aims to expand across Central Asia, beginning with Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan and extending to neighboring markets such as Kazakhstan, and into Southeast Asia, particularly Vietnam and Indonesia. It says demand for education infrastructure modernization, digital transformation and vocational education is growing in both regions. The company is seeking government and public-sector organizations, schools, universities and vocational training institutions, local EdTech and educational equipment companies, local partners experienced in ODA and public education projects, and systems integration (SI) and distribution partners able to handle installation, training and maintenance. It gives priority to long-term partners that can support pilot projects, localization, deployment and operation rather than simple product distribution.

The 57th Korea Electronics Show (KES 2026) ran from Oct. 13 (Tuesday) to 16 (Friday) in Halls A and B at COEX in Seoul. The Korea Electronics Association (KEA) organized the show, and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources hosted it. The KES website lists 500 exhibitors and 1,100 booths. Its themes included electronic parts and materials such as sensors, connectors, printed circuit boards (PCBs) and power supplies; AI transformation (AX) fields such as generative AI, on-device AI, AI chips and smart home and wearable devices; mobility; robotics; digital health; ESG; and Web 3.0 and XR. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event featured X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony took place on Oct. 13.
